prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: C01-CH07-S33-EST, 七塔王城终局远景, a full authored opaque narrative setting plate. Native wide 16:9 landscape, preferably 1672×941. Fill the canvas; no frame or text.
Reference roles: Image 1 and Image 2 are APPROVED STYLE examples only: chunky matte broad color planes, strong simple silhouettes and economical outlines. Image 3 is the ORIGINAL exact source slot, used ONLY to retain its nighttime walled-capital subject, elevated three-quarter camera, enclosing water, approach bridge, layered urban depth and tower hierarchy. Do not copy its fine-grained clutter, tiny textures or large number of equal-height towers.
Scene: the seven-tower capital at the opening of the final chapter, viewed from an elevated approach at blue dusk. An inhabited monumental city awaits the final confrontation. This is an establishing setting, not a victory celebration or the ending choice. Cool slate masonry, muted blue roof masses, tiny restrained warm windows and torches, dark green surrounding tree shapes and distant blue hills. River curls around the city's lower edge. A broad old west-wall road approaches from the lower left; a south river-gate bridge crosses the water near center front; a third narrower road bends toward the rear northern tower quarter. The city contains distinct low house blocks, one long hospital hall with warm windows, a few broad grain-store roofs, a water basin and broad streets. Buildings are simple large shapes and visibly inhabited; no catastrophe, no burning neighborhoods.
Composition: EXACTLY SEVEN clearly separate monumental oath-tower silhouettes form the skyline, with open blue sky separating all seven tops. These are the seven principal towers, each thick and readable, not seven needles. Arrange three on the left, one tallest at center, three on the right at staggered depths and different heights. The center tower rises from a wide stepped palace building and has a flat round battlement crown of stone masonry, NOT a metal crown motif. The six others have distinct but related broad roof or battlement profiles, one modest dome, one blunt gable, one flat octagonal parapet, one low dark conical roof, another paired-shoulder profile that remains ONE building, one squat round turret. These architectural variations should be modest and structurally credible. Keep lower city and wall towers short enough that they cannot be mistaken for the seven tall principal towers. No extra spires, needles, finials or large banner poles. Leave 45 native pixels of sky above every tower top and sufficient breathing room at left and right. The front arched gate and its low square gatehouse anchor the center. Large wall ribbons and water shape lead inward toward the tall central palace tower. Broad streets and roofs fill the lower two thirds. Make the central gate-palace axis legible even in a portrait center crop, while the full wide view clearly preserves all seven skyline towers.
Style and hierarchy: same cheerful but grounded tactical-fantasy illustration family as the approved references, rendered with chunky matte shapes, two or three tonal values per material, crisp dark outer contours, simplified broad stone planes and simple roof blocks. The mood is quiet, serious blue evening; keep the buildings clearly readable, not almost black. Limited muted blue, slate gray, deep green and warm amber accents. Greatly reduce the old source's detail density. Do not render individual shingles, hundreds of brick chips, tiny cobbles, scratches or endless window grids. The 256×144 reduction must still show seven towers, a walled living city and the river gate.
Constraints: opaque full scene, no transparent canvas. No readable text, runes, labels, user interface, watermark, decorative border or panel grid. No named people, dragon, giant floating crown, enslaved army, synchronized kneeling, victory parade or dominant unified flag. No city-destroying fire, laser beams, magical forcefield, neon glow, glossy 3D, photorealism, grain or fine crosshatching.
